body.p: An Evenk met ogres. He had a younger sibling, a girl. They made their camp together. They stayed for one day, at the place, where they were staying, they married the girl to a man. That man gave his younger sister, he exchanged, for his younger sister he took the woman. Then he separated, he went off separately, he wandered off. The ogres went off separately, the father of the ogre respected his daughter-in-law, he didn't make her work. He made a yurt for his daughter-in-law, for that she eats separately, he killed a fat reindeer. Then in the night the woman's husband is crying, the woman says: "Why are you crying?" Her husband doesn't tell. Once the woman lay down to sleep in the evening. When she had fallen asleep, girls came. "Aunt", they said, "I'll play with you knucklebones". The woman said: "What will be with me, if you take [them], how will you take my knucklebones?" [DCh]: Ending -s for 2SG is unexpected after zero aorist, but there is no other tense marker. "Aunt, they sacrifice you". "You all will play with my knucklebones. How will they sacrifice me?" "Aunt, they want to kill you now". There the woman said: "My little one, go home, you eat me [then]". The girls went off. When they had gone off, [the woman] dressed quickly, she put rotten wood under the blanket, she went along her path, she came back. Having taken her skies, they went along her path and saw a bent larch, she climbed onto its top. There on the top she sat down. She heard, how they started shamanizing, they came in order to kill her, they pierced a glaive through the yurt, they pierced the woman. When that one cracked, they said: "Well, may she suffer, we kill her now". They looked at her, and it is rotten wood. Then they beat the girl and said: "Who has said it, tell". That one told: "She said it, she said it". They killed one girl as a sacrifice. Then they looked with fires for the traces of the woman, they found her path, they went along it, they went along the path with fires, they came to a tree, her trace disappeared. They went around, her trace is not there, her trace is nowhere. "Tomorrow we'll find her, she won't escape, tomorrow we'll find her!" The men [DCh]: Is "ÉtÉËn" really NEG-FUT.IMM-3SG? (cf. Vasilevich 1958: 730f. 'forma tverdoj voli') went home. The woman looked down from the treetop. When all had lain down to sleep, the woman jumped into the snow. She crawled under the snow, she was crawling for a long time. Then she jumped out of the snow, she put on her skies, she went to his elder brother, she followed his path. She went for a long time, early in the morning she caught him up. Having caught up her elder brother, she started to cry, the brother said: "Why are you crying?" "To what kind of a devil did you give [me]! They wanted to sacrify me, they were about to eat me, I went away from there". Her brother got angry, he killed his wife, he put on his younger sister's clothes, he flayed her face, left it in the tent, he said to the sister: "Wander off, if I don't come within three day, say [that] I was killed". The man [hid] so that he saw the yurt, he watched the coming ogres, who were following her. He watched the way of the chasing people, he was about to shoot at them. They came at midday, they chased [her]. Having come they saw the killed woman, they said: "What a good man, but why didn't you run away?" [GVY:] Unclear: the woman's brother did escape. They flayed her. They lit a fire, they fried her meat in order to eat it. When they were eating, the father [felt] his heart, when eating the woman he said: "Something touches my heart. Isn't she our?" His relatives said: "Don't be nuts, eat!" [DCh]: Is "bihi" really connegative form? They started to discuss: "Do we hunt this man or not?" Some of them said: "Why should we chase a good man, he has killed the one we were chasing". When they were talking so, that man silently went away. Having gone a bit, he drove with skiers along the path. He went along the path for a long time, he came to the camp of his younger sister. He came there and drank tea. Drinking tea he saw [that] three men were going through the lowland on the other side. The man caught a calf, he killed it, quickly he took its shoulder blade. He started to tell fortunes out of it. The shoulder blade broke immediately. The man went [GVY:] tarinÅá» = tariÅá»n?off, he went to kill those ones. One man went out. He shot at the leaving one, he shot through his eyes. That one called his friends: "They shot at me (?)!" [DCh]: Not finally clear who is shooting. The man shot again and killed him. Then the others came, then came on skiers and said: "Who has killed the master?" The man watched the coming people, he shot into the heart of the front one, that one fell down. The man also shot immediately, he killed three men. He came home, then he wandered off.
